## Database comparison

| Criterion | Azure SQL Database | PostgreSQL Flexible | Cosmos DB |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fit with .NET | Native: EF Core and SqlClient first-class | Good: Npgsql EF Core provider | SDK only, not relational |
| Column encryption admins cannot read | Always Encrypted (client-side keys; VBS enclaves for range and LIKE) | None built in; application-level encryption needed | Client-side encryption via SDK |
| Tamper-evident history | Ledger tables, cryptographic digests | pgaudit logs, not cryptographic | No |
| Row-level security for tenants | Yes, security predicates | Yes, RLS policies | No (partition keys) |
| Dynamic data masking | Built in | Views or extensions | No |
| Entra-only auth + managed identity | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Customer-managed keys | TDE with CMK, database-level CMK | CMK with auto-rotation | CMK |
| Threat detection | Defender for SQL | Defender for open-source databases | Defender for Cosmos DB |
| Relational clinical + billing model | Yes | Yes | Poor fit |
| Verdict | Chosen | Strong alternative | Not for core data |

## Twelve layers of data protection (in place before the first real record in P1)

| # | Layer | Control |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | Network | Private endpoint only; public network access disabled; App Service VNet integration; no IP firewall exceptions |
| 02 | Who can connect | Microsoft Entra authentication only; the API uses a managed identity; separate least-privilege database users per module and for migrations; no standing human access (just-in-time elevation) |
| 03 | Encryption at rest | TDE with a customer-managed key in Key Vault or Managed HSM, automatic rotation; backups and Blob Storage under the same key policy |
| 04 | Encryption in use | Always Encrypted on Aadhaar, Emirates ID, passport, ABHA and insurance member numbers; column master key usable only by the API identity, so database admins and Medvya staff see ciphertext |
| 05 | In transit | TLS 1.2+ (1.3 where supported), Encrypt=Strict connections, HSTS on all web endpoints |
| 06 | Row access | Row-level security predicate on tenant_id set through SESSION_CONTEXT per request, plus EF Core query filters; cross-tenant tests in CI |
| 07 | Masking | Dynamic data masking on phone, email and date of birth for support and reporting roles |
| 08 | Tamper evidence | Ledger tables for audit events, signed notes, consents and invoices; digests stored in immutable Blob Storage and verified on schedule |
| 09 | Monitoring | Azure SQL auditing to Log Analytics and immutable storage; Defender for SQL alerts on injection and anomalous access; alert on bulk reads and exports |
| 10 | Backup and recovery | Point-in-time restore (up to 35 days), long-term retention per country rule, backups kept in-country, monthly restore drill |
| 11 | Application | Parameterised queries only (EF Core/Dapper), no dynamic SQL, input validation, rate limits, watermarked exports |
| 12 | Secrets | Key Vault with RBAC, soft delete and purge protection; GitHub OIDC to Azure; no secrets in code or config files |

**Per country and per customer:** one logical server per country (Central India, UAE North), each with its own keys, backups and logs. Clinics share an elastic pool, separated by row-level security. From P7, hospitals get a dedicated database and their own customer-managed key. No patient data crosses countries.
